newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank sector pay talks begin.
newsitem.headline: German bank sector pay talks begin.

text.p: New talks between Germany's banking employers and the main trade unions in the sector began on Wednesday aimed at solving a dispute over sick pay entitlements for the 450,000 workers in the industry.

Horst Mueller, chief negotiator for the Federation of Banking Employers said that if trade unions continued to insist on sick pay entitlements at 100 percent of salary, it would demand compensating reductions in other areas of labour costs.

The second round of talks follows an earlier meeting between employers and the DAG and HBV unions in December at which employers agreed to continue to pay full sick pay until a wider contractual agreeement was reached in the sector.

Germany's banks had earlier implemented a new law, introduced last October, allowing them to cut sick pay to 80 percent of salary but met strong resistance. Some 15,000 workers took part in a day of walk-outs and protests.
Mueller said before the talks started that the negotiators would aim to produce new employee contracts "that can lead us into the year 2000".

"It is no longer in accord with the times that a bank employee can earn more money simply because he sits in his chair and gets older," Mueller, also a board member of Dresdner Bank AG, Germany's second largest bank, said.
A spokesman for the HBV banking and insurance union said that it was looking for a 1997 pay rise of between 3.6 and 3.8 percent.
